Packaging claim: Hidden Road Loops Control the Traffic Light
Core fact: Many intersections use inductive-loop detectors: loops of wire embedded in pavement sense the presence of a conductive metal vehicle.
Second reveal: The traffic controller can use that detection as an input for an actuated signal instead of relying only on a fixed timer.
First-frame and mechanism proof: Visible rectangular saw cuts/loops in the lane at a red light, then a car stopping over them.
Search queries: inductive loop traffic signal pavement; road sensor loop intersection; car detector traffic light
Fact boundaries: Do not claim all traffic lights use loops or that a loop always changes the light immediately; intersections may use cameras, radar, fixed timing, or other logic.
